Tossed
tŏst
v. (past participle of toss: thrown about, agitated; rendering Hebrew sa'ar and na'ar, Greek kludonizomai, rhipizo, basanizo, and cheimazo)
Middle English tossen, of uncertain origin, perhaps Scandinavian. The New Testament's four Greek words are all pictures of water and weather.

Biblical Definition

The word belongs to the sea. The disciples' ship was “tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary” (Mat 14:24); Paul's was “exceedingly tossed with a tempest” (Act 27:18). Paul makes it a picture of the immature church: “that we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine” (Eph 4:14). James makes it the double-minded man at prayer: “he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed” (Jas 1:6). And God speaks to His people by it: “O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours” (Isa 54:11). David: “I am tossed up and down as the locust” (Psa 109:23); Solomon: treasures gotten by lying “are a vanity tossed to and fro” (Pro 21:6).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines toss as to throw with the hand; to lift with a sudden motion; to agitate; to make restless; to be tossed, to be agitated as by waves.

expand to see more

TOSS, v.t. To throw with the hand; particularly, to throw with the palm of the hand upward.

2. To throw with violence.

3. To agitate; to make restless; as, calumny tosses the mind.

4. To keep in play; to tumble over; as, to spend four years in tossing the rules of grammar.

Key Scripture

Eph 4:14 — "That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive;"

Jas 1:6 — "But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed."

Isa 54:11 — "O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires."

Mat 14:24 — "But the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves: for the wind was contrary."

Act 27:18 — "And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next day they lightened the ship;"

Pro 21:6 — "The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death."

Modern Corruption

Doctrinal instability is admired as open-mindedness, and Paul calls it childhood and gives the church a ministry to grow out of it.

expand to see more

Ephesians 4:14 names as a defect what the age names as a virtue. To be tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine is, in the modern church, to be on a journey, to be humble about one's certainties, to be always learning; Paul calls it being children, and adds that the winds are blown “by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive.” The remedy is in the verses before: Christ gave pastors and teachers “till we all come in the unity of the faith… unto a perfect man.” Settled doctrine is not the enemy of growth; it is what growth is for. A man who is still tossed after twenty years of preaching has either had no pastors or has refused them.

James 1:6 puts the tossing inside the man. The double-minded asker is a wave — not a rock in the wave but the wave itself — driven and tossed, and James says plainly, “let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.” The failure is not too little feeling but two minds, and prayer offered from two minds is offered to no one in particular. Isaiah 54:11 is the other side of every sea-verse in the Bible: the One who lets His people be tossed with tempest is the One who speaks to them in it, and the promise that follows is a city built of sapphires.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sa'ar (H5590), to storm, be tempest-tossed; na'ar (H5287), to shake off; Greek kludonizomai (G2831), to be tossed by waves; rhipizo (G4494), to fan, toss; basanizo (G928), to distress; cheimazo (G5492), to be storm-driven.

expand to see more

Hebrew sa'ar (H5590) — to be tossed by tempest; Isaiah 54:11; na'ar (H5287), Psalm 109:23; nadaph (H5086), Proverbs 21:6.

Greek kludonizomai (G2831) — to be tossed by waves; Ephesians 4:14 only; rhipizo (G4494), James 1:6 only.

Greek basanizo (G928) — to toss, torment; Matthew 14:24; cheimazo (G5492), Acts 27:18 only.

Usage

"“Tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine” — childhood, not humility."

"“Like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed” — the double-minded at prayer."

"“O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted” — and then the sapphires."
